data.title: Build Neon: The Glowing Element
data.description: Discover how protons, neutrons, and electrons build the glowing neon gas found in bright city signs.

challenges.instruction: Add 10 protons to the nucleus to create the element Neon. Don't forget to balance it with 10 neutrons and 10 electrons!
challenges.hint: Check the atomic number of Neon on the periodic table—it is 10!
challenges.narration: Amazing! 10 protons defines Neon, the noble gas that makes brilliant red and orange signs glow!

challenges.instruction: Examine this mysterious atom with 8 protons, 8 neutrons, and 8 electrons. What element have we built?
challenges.hint: Look at the atomic number. Which element has 8 protons?
challenges.narration: Spot on! That is Oxygen, the vital gas you breathe every second to keep your body moving.

challenges.instruction: Fill the electron shells for Neon following the rules: 2 electrons in the first shell, and the remaining 8 in the second shell.
challenges.hint: The first shell holds a maximum of 2, and the second shell can hold up to 8.
challenges.narration: See how its outer valence shell is completely full? That stable electron configuration is why neon doesn't like to react with other elements!

challenges.instruction: Start with a neutral Sodium atom (11 protons, 12 neutrons, 11 electrons) and remove 1 electron to form a sodium ion.
challenges.hint: Sodium has 11 protons. To make an ion with a +1 charge, you need one fewer electron than protons.
challenges.narration: You removed an electron and created a sodium cation with a positive charge! That is exactly what happens when table salt dissolves in water.

challenges.instruction: Build Carbon-14! Start with standard carbon (6 protons, 6 electrons), but adjust the neutrons to make this famous radioactive isotope used in archaeology.
challenges.hint: Carbon always has 6 protons, but carbon-14 has a mass number of 14.
challenges.narration: Brilliant! You built Carbon-14, an isotope with extra neutrons that scientists use to date ancient artifacts and fossils.
